summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with fever and cough three days after placement of a central venous line, initially thought to be a port but appearing as a tunneled Hickman line. She also presented with neck pain at the line site, wheezing, and asthma exacerbation. Workup revealed no bacterial infection—chest X-ray was clear, blood cultures negative, and urine culture showed only contaminant flora. Symptoms were attributed to likely viral bronchitis. She was treated with nebulizers and a 7-day course of oral prednisone for asthma, which improved her respiratory status. Prednisone caused hyperglycemia, requiring adjustment of her U500 insulin regimen under endocrinology guidance. Her blood sugars stabilized, and she was discharged home with instructions to continue steroids, monitor glucose, and follow up. She refused a discharge exam but was alert, afebrile, and breathing comfortably.
problems: Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
